## Where a model matrix meets the view-projection

16 instances, pass 1 only — pass 2 grows with the instances too and swamps the
difference. A MATMUL costs 64, a MATVEC 16, a global access 100.

| Vertices an instance | Per-vertex | Composed | Composing |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 105,216 | 154,080 | **+46.4%** |
| 32 | 400,896 | 437,472 | **+9.1%** |
| 64 | 801,792 | 821,984 | **+2.5%** |
| 96 | 1,202,688 | 1,206,496 | **+0.3%** |
| 128 | 1,603,584 | 1,591,008 | **-0.8%** |
| 256 | 3,207,168 | 3,129,056 | **-2.4%** |
| 512 | 6,414,336 | 6,205,152 | **-3.3%** |

The arithmetic predicts a crossing at four vertices an instance: a MATMUL is
four MATVECs, so folding once should beat an extra MATVEC at every vertex past
four of them. It is two orders out, because the pass is not its multiply —
sixteen floats read and sixteen written cost 3,200 around a MATMUL of 64, and
pass 1 pays nothing at all for its matrix, the constant window handing a block
one for the whole warp.
